newsitem.title: SPAIN: Seat makes profit after 3 years of losses.
newsitem.headline: Seat makes profit after 3 years of losses.

text.p: Volkswagen AG's Spanish subsidiary Seat said on Tuesday it made a net profit of 5.34 billion pesetas ($37.3 million) in 1996 after three years of heavy losses.
Seat's performance was boosted by a series of exceptional items, including asset sales and subsidies, but the firm said it hoped to make a profit on the strength of its own operations in 1997.

"It's still early to make forecasts for 1997 but our target is to reach profits without any external aid and, according to data from the first part of the year, we seem to be in a position to do it," chairman Alain de Smedt told a news conference.
In the two months to February this year, Seat's sales rose 32.5 percent to 114.84 billion pesetas. Sales in 1996 rose to 607.3 billion pesetas from 456.52 billion in 1995.

Extraordinary profit jumped 12 billion pesetas to 42.1 billion. The breakdown of exceptionals showed about eight billion pesetas income from asset sales and 14.2 billion in regional and central government subsidies.

Of the remaining 20.5 billion pesetas, around five billion was due to fewer provisions. The rest of the income came primarily from parent Volkswagen, although the firm declined to specify exactly what the figure was.
"Volkswagen's contributions to Seat form part of that 20.5 billion pesetas, but I won't give the exact figure as that's an internal affair," finance director Utz Claassen said.
SEAT aims to raise production by more than 10 percent this year to 460,000 units, with sales growing at the same rate.
De Smedt reaffirmed plans for investment to rise to 120 billion pesetas between 1997 and the year 2000 with the outlay financed by cash flow.

Seat's return to profits in 1996 marks the end of a black period in which its worst performance showed losses of 151.32 billion pesetas in 1993. Those were reduced to losses of 29.47 billion in 1994 and 11.29 billion in 1995.
The firm underwent a restructuring, which included concentration of production at its Martorell plant in Catalonia, as well as the sale of its Navarre plant to Volkswagen.
After the restructuring, the number of Seat employees has fallen to roughly 12,900 from more than 20,000 workers. ($ = 143.1 Spanish Pesetas)
